data.long_meaning: In the Kikuyu language, Nyambura means 'Mother of the Rock'. This name is derived from the revered goddess Nyamira, who is believed to be the protector of fertility and the giver of life. The name Nyambura is often given to girls as a symbol of strength and resilience, reflecting the unwavering support of a mother. The name Nyambura carries the meaning “Mother of the Rock” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Nyambura usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of the rock and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Nyambura represents the unwavering love and support of a mother, embodying the spiritual qualities of nurturing, protection, and strength.
data.etymology: Nyambura belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of the Rock.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nyambura total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nyambura holds cultural significance among the Kikuyu people of Eastern Africa. It reinforces the importance of motherhood and the role of women in nurturing and caring for their children. Nyambura also carries a sense of connection to the rich traditions and heritage of the Kikuyu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual sense, Nyambura represents the unfailing love and protection of a divine feminine presence. As a name derived from Nyamira, the goddess of fertility and life, Nyambura reminds us of the cyclical nature of life, the power of nurturing, and the strength that comes from being a mother figure or support system. The name encourages reverence for the feminine divine and a deep appreciation for the role mothers play in shaping the lives of their children.
